Latin → Urdu script

Type Brahui in Brolikva Latin. You get the orthography to store and a fully vocalized string an Urdu TTS voice can read correctly.

IPA
/ /
Brahui orthography — store this
 
Vocalized for TTS — send this to the voice
 
Respelled — diacritic-stripping fallback
 
Devanagari — what a Hindi voice is sent
 
English respelling
 
ASCII accepted: sh=ş · zh=ź · LH=ļ · GH=ģ · T=ŧ · D=đ · R=ŕ · N=ń · aa=á · ii=í · uu=ú.
Not shortcuts, because they destroyed real contrasts: tt dd rr are genuine geminates (baŧŧa, izzat) and kh gh ch are aspirated loan consonants (khuriyá, bhallo). For /x/ and /ɣ/ type x and ģ.

Urdu script → Latin

Paste Brahui written in Perso-Arabic script and read it back.

Brahui — Latin
 
Say as
 
IPA
 
Why the diacritics matter. Urdu text normally omits short-vowel marks and a TTS engine guesses them from its own Urdu lexicon — which contains no Brahui words. Every output here is fully vocalized (zabar / zer / pesh / sukun) so the engine reads exactly what is written and the long–short vowel contrast survives.

Add a word

Write it in script or in Latin — each fills the other. The Latin is the source of truth; script and IPA are regenerated on every read.

Say as
 

Bulk add

One meaning = brahui per line, script or Latin.

Your progress

Progress lives in this browser only. Save it to a file to keep it through a browser reset, or to carry it to another machine.

Export & reset the word list

The review sheet puts every unverified row in front of a Brahui speaker first.

Sources

Connected speech, not isolated words — intonation is where a word list stops helping.

Practice
Voice settings
Prepared Lekha audio is the fast, consistent default.

Uses the recorded Brahui library immediately. It never scans, switches to, or waits for a device voice.

A silence after each word, so a phrase or an example sentence can be followed word by word instead of arriving as one run. Set it to 0 for natural, connected speech. A single word is unaffected either way.
